explanations: Soda–lime, containing around 70% silica, accounts for around 90% of modern manufactured glass.
Archaeological evidence puts its making back to at least 3600 BC, in Mesopotamia, Egypt or Syria; the earliest known objects were beads.
Some kinds occur naturally: obsidian is volcanic, and has been used for arrowheads and knives since the Stone Age.
It can be coloured by adding metal salts, or painted with vitreous enamels, which is how stained windows are made.
It is an amorphous, non-crystalline solid, often transparent and chemically inert, most often formed by rapidly cooling the molten form.

sources.excerpt: Soda–lime glass, containing around 70% silica, accounts for around 90% of modern manufactured glass.
Archaeological evidence suggests glassmaking dates back to at least 3600 BC in Mesopotamia, Egypt, or Syria.
Some glasses such as volcanic glass are naturally occurring, and obsidian has been used to make arrowheads and knives since the Stone Age.
Glass can be coloured by adding metal salts or painted and printed with vitreous enamels, leading to its use in stained glass windows and other glass art objects.
Glass is most often formed by rapid cooling (quenching) of the molten form.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: obsidian is one natural form and appears in clue three as an example, not as the answer; quartz and silica are ingredients rather than the material; a crystal is by definition ordered, which the first and last clues rule out.
